## ADR-025 — Durable user-derived embeddings prohibited for the current release
**Status:** ACCEPTED · 2026-10-04

**Decision.** **Durable user-derived embeddings are prohibited on both server
and device for the current release.** This includes vectors derived from a
user's transactions, selected merchants, memos and assistant conversations,
and encoded, quantized, reduced or purportedly anonymised forms of those vectors.
No vector extension, user-derived embedding column, vector datastore, provider,
model contract or spend is authorized. Accepting this prohibited option does
not turn the previous default denial into permission to persist.

The deterministic-first categorisation baseline is unchanged.
Retrieval-augmented authoritative financial arithmetic is prohibited.

**Authority and acceptance.** The coordinating Sprint completion session
`5a1e7d78-6f81-4abb-9ab5-d8b1648df012` selected the conservative prohibited option
under the owner's general autonomous original-backlog delivery delegation and
confirmed the owner-published `coordinator-embeddings-source-ready-20261004`
addendum to [#56](https://github.com/PenniLogic/docs/issues/56). This is not a
bespoke owner embedding attestation. The ACCEPTED header and generated registry
entry are a **source proposal on the author branch**, becoming accepted source
only after separate current-head review and protected merge. They are not
runtime enforcement, independent approval or completion of the original issue.

AC2 and DoD3 remain UNMET: no actual database-extension gate consumes this artifact.

**Allocation and scope.** The coordinator authorized only the appended ADR-025
allocation for original `T-ADR-EMBED-12`, above accepted ADR-024, using
[LAYOUT.md](LAYOUT.md)'s unchanged layout-owner bootstrap and ticket-scoped
generator. ADR-001..024, all old allocations, old registry entries, original
index slots and manual text are preserved from the accepted base. ADR-022's
source decision is now accepted; this source neither changes it nor claims its
runtime controls are implemented. Global AI egress and custom destinations
remain OFF. The original issue remains open and its assigned `Future` sprint is
unchanged.

### 1. Why prohibit persistence

An embedding of personal financial text is **personal financial data**, not a
safe substitute for the text. A similarity-searchable representation preserves
information useful for inference; removing an owner identifier does not remove
that information. Adding a second derived datastore also adds copies and an
erasure path outside the guarantees consumers already owe
[ADR-018](ADR-018.md) and [ADR-021](ADR-021.md).

The product is useful without that store. Deterministic merchant rules,
append-only categorisation under [ADR-016](ADR-016.md), user clarification and
the deterministic debt/ledger engines remain the baseline. Static, non-user
category assets and strictly operation-local optional inference can be bounded
without retaining a user's vectors. Their classification is not permission to
activate a model: this decision selects no model, dimension, license or provider.
Research recommendations and historical prices are not approved procurement
or privacy evidence.

The [AI research correction banner](../ai/01-ai-harness-research.md#correction-banner--read-before-acting-on-this-document)
already treats persisted embeddings and vector extensions as unapproved options.
This chooses that original ticket's explicit prohibition, not a replacement
framework or a postponed default-on feature.

| Option | Disposition |
|---|---|
| Prohibit durable user-derived vectors; distinguish static assets and operation-local inference | **Chosen.** Preserves default denial and existing erasure guarantees without a new datastore, external data purpose or spend. |
| Persist user-derived vectors in a server vector database | **Rejected.** Adds inversion and membership disclosure, tenant/query admission and hard-delete/restore obligations without accepted evidence or an owning gate. |
| Persist only on the device or in a short-lived cache | **Rejected.** Device files, offline stores, cache snapshots and backups are still durable copies; a short TTL or a zero-day retention label is not non-persistence. |
| Encrypt, quantize, hash or call the retained vectors anonymous | **Rejected.** Does not establish safe similarity search, eliminate inference or erase independent copies; see section 4. |
| Hide embeddings in conversation history, transaction enrichment or a learned prototype | **Rejected.** Cross-purpose reuse and a misleading static label bypass the decision rather than satisfy it. |
| Leave an extension installed but promise not to use it | **Rejected.** The original allowlist criterion concerns admission before data exists, not an operator's intent or the current absence of a vector table. |

### 2. Classes, permitted memory and copy boundaries

These are **data-treatment classes**, not three implemented features.

| Class | Provenance and purpose | Permitted location and lifetime |
|---|---|---|
| `STATIC_CATEGORY_PROTOTYPE` | Reviewed product category/reference text that is not derived from any user's data, custom label, selected merchant, correction, conversation or aggregation of users. Category matching only. | A versioned, read-only product asset, which may be bundled on server/device. Ordinary non-user asset lifecycle; no user retention/erasure obligation is invented. |
| `EPHEMERAL_USER_INFERENCE` | A user's transaction, merchant, memo or conversation vector, for one authorized categorisation or purpose-scoped assistant operation. | Only that server request's or device operation's non-durable memory; no other request, tenant, session or purpose may reuse it. End on success, cancellation, timeout or error. |
| `DURABLE_USER_DERIVED` | The same user sources, including transformed vectors and user-conditioned prototypes. | **No permitted store, model version or retention period.** Prevention of creation, not a zero-day collection policy or a new crypto-shredding classification. |

**Static lineage is substantive.** A globally known merchant reference is not
the same thing as a particular user's choice to transact with that merchant.
A vector learned from the latter remains user-derived even if the dictionary
already contains the merchant. User feedback, custom categories and pooled
user examples must not update or fine-tune the static asset. Existing explicit
structured merchant rules may still record ordinary user corrections under
their own contracts; that is not vector training. A runtime cannot accept a
client's `static` label as lineage proof.

**Model admission remains separate.** Every class's `permitted_model_versions`
is empty because no model is approved here. A separately reviewed model/asset
manifest must pin an actual supported model revision, representation and
compatible prototype generation before optional inference; unknown model
versions, dimensions, assets, provenance or purposes fail closed. No model name,
license or dimension is guessed. Updating a genuinely non-user static asset
does not authorize indexing user data.

**Ephemeral means no durable escape.** No user-derived vector enters a server
or device database, file, persistent or cross-request cache, export, replica,
backup, log, trace, analytics event, queue/job payload, vector/search index,
swap/hibernation image, crash dump, training/fine-tuning corpus, re-index input
or checkpoint, or provider retention. Serialization as an array, JSON, bytes,
ciphertext or a non-vector column is not an exception. Neither a TTL nor
encryption makes a durable cache ephemeral.

Optional execution must be bounded by its declared request timeout, quota and
memory limits, scoped to one admitted tenant and purpose, and release all
request references, tensors and work on every end condition. It cannot queue a
vector for later work, retain an in-memory session cache or allow an in-flight
job to recreate data after cancellation/erasure. The consumer must demonstrate
that its runtime does not spill or dump these values. Reference release is not
a claim of physical zeroisation by a garbage collector or protection against
an already compromised process. **If non-durable execution or its bounds cannot
be established, deny optional inference and keep the deterministic baseline.**

This adds no egress permission. Any independently admitted server inference
still obeys existing minimisation, provider retention/training, entitlements
and backend-only routing controls; an unavailable or unapproved egress path
remains denied. Device-local inference is not client-direct provider access.
Optional permissions may be denied without losing manual entry or core use.
No new retention, logging payload, provider or inference call is implemented.

### 3. Conversation and enrichment purpose separation

**Conversation history and transaction enrichment may not share an embedding
store, vector collection or unscoped payload cache.** No embeddings are
persisted for either purpose, and operation-local vectors cannot be copied
from one purpose's request to the other. Conversation-derived merchant vectors
cannot enter a dictionary, enrichment result, retained assistant memory or
training/re-index corpus.

The [product's AI contract](../product/01-product-spec.md#37-ai) remains unchanged:
history is off by default; opted-in ordinary history is core-API-owned,
encrypted, retention-bounded, exportable/deletable and never used for training;
the AI service is stateless. History consent, a family grant or an enrichment
request authorizes none of the forbidden derived copies.

This decision does not require a new database engine for ordinary encrypted
history and structured transaction records or redefine their existing physical
database co-location. They remain separately purpose-scoped records under their
existing consent, encryption, RLS, retention and erasure contracts. An existing
core API database is not a shared logical embedding store or permission to
mix their payloads. ADR-005's default-deny sharing and ADR-018/021's grant,
key and erasure rules are not loosened.

The model may explain deterministic tool results, never calculate authoritative
balances, totals, interest or payoff dates through retrieval or its own output.
Money remains server-authoritative integer minor units plus currency. The
[research grounding boundary](../ai/01-ai-harness-research.md#62-why-llms-must-never-do-financial-arithmetic)
and [product advice boundary](../product/01-product-spec.md#23-suggest-to-find-a-job-which-has-x-salary-vs-financial-advice-regulation)
remain intact; a retrieved example or disclaimer cannot become authority.

### 4. Inversion, membership inference and erasure threat reasoning

This is an **author source threat analysis**, not a measured attack experiment
or separate Security/Privacy approval. No live vector, real user text, model
performance percentage or empirical disclosure bound is supplied.

| Adversary capability and path | Disclosure or failure | Decision consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Read vectors from a database/device dump, retained cache, support dump, backup or provider copy; know or obtain the embedding model | Approximate inversion can reconstruct or infer identifying merchant/memo/conversation content or sensitive financial attributes. It need not recover every original byte to disclose a person. | Treat user vectors as personal financial data; deny every durable copy rather than classify the vector as anonymous reference data. |
| Submit candidate text to an embedding model and compare distances, exposed scores or nearest-neighbour responses | Membership inference can reveal that a candidate transaction, merchant or conversation occurred; repeated/adaptive queries can narrow the evidence. No exact text inversion is necessary. | No retained user vector set or shared query surface. A future proposal must test its actual model and exposed interface, not infer safety from low reconstruction quality alone. |
| Bypass tenant filters, use a broadly privileged maintenance role or query a mixed conversation/enrichment index | Cross-tenant disclosure and cross-purpose profiling; owner identifiers or a category label need not accompany every returned vector to make correlation possible. | No durable user vector store; operation-local values stay tenant/purpose scoped. Future tenancy and purpose tests must cover all roles and negative query paths. |
| Delete a primary row or destroy the user's DEK while an index, quantized copy, queue, export, replica or backup remains | A derived representation may remain searchable/recoverable or be rebuilt by a stale job. A provider or device copy may not use the user's DEK at all. | Prevention is the current mechanism. Any future persistence requires verified hard deletion, post-erasure similarity residue queries and restore/re-index barriers over every copy. |
| Relabel user-conditioned vectors as static, retain them through errors, or export an operation's tensors in diagnostics | The static/ephemeral exception becomes a hidden persistent user dataset. | Require actual provenance and non-spill evidence before optional execution; keep denied-path diagnostics content-free. |

Ordinary application-layer authenticated encryption prevents ordinary similarity
indexing over the encrypted representation. Decrypting vectors for search,
keeping a plaintext/quantized side index, or encrypting only the original text
restores the disclosure surface. Storage encryption protects offline access
only while its key/access boundary holds; it does not protect against an
authorized similarity-query role, a compromised runtime or provider retention.
No specialised searchable-encryption scheme is approved by this record.

**Crypto-shredding alone is explicitly insufficient for persisted searchable
user vectors.** A DEK deletion cannot erase plaintext indexes or copies under
another key, undo earlier inference, or attest that provider copies are gone.
Even the accepted encrypted-text design publishes its backup-retention residue:
ADR-018 sections 6.6-6.7 and ADR-021 sections 3.7/4.2 require replay before
readiness and do not claim that a pre-erasure backup instantly disappears.
Those existing residue statements remain unchanged; this ADR creates no
embedding-specific exception to them.

While persistence is prohibited, store/tenant/network selection, persistent
model/dimension pins, full re-index conformance, live similarity serving and
post-erasure vector-query execution are conditional N/A. **They were not
simulated or run.** No store exists here to produce vector counts by model
version, stale-generation counts, residue results or cross-tenant denial rates.
Future persistence must publish those observability requirements.

An accidental prohibited copy is an incident, not retroactive authorization:
stop the relevant serving/writer/rebuild paths, inventory copies and coordinate
verified cleanup with the existing ADR-021 erasure/restore owners. Do not claim
key destruction alone removes the residue, erase ledger/audit history, or let
a repair job silently recreate a vector. This source unit performs no incident
deletion and changes no erasure implementation.

### 7. Future reversal and default-off implementation

`embedding-reopening-v1` requires **all** the following evidence; elapsed time,
a research recommendation, consent, better storage encryption or a cheaper
model is not a reopening decision.

| Evidence identifier | Testable condition |
|---|---|
| `REOPEN-NEED-MINIMISATION` | Reproduce benefit against deterministic-first and operation-local alternatives using predeclared numeric thresholds and a minimal purpose/copy inventory. |
| `REOPEN-INVERSION-MEMBERSHIP` | Model/interface-specific inversion and membership review, adversary capabilities and predeclared numeric disclosure limits with measured results meeting them. |
| `REOPEN-TENANCY-PROTECTION` | Named store/network/tenant boundary, least-privilege roles, RLS where applicable and negative tenant/grant/purpose tests reconciled with ADR-018. |
| `REOPEN-MODEL-REINDEX` | Exact model revision, license, dimension and representation; complete verified re-index with atomic generation switch and no mixed generations. |
| `REOPEN-RETENTION-ERASURE` | Sourced retention/export, hard deletion of all copies, post-erasure similarity residue queries, provider obligations and backup/restore/rebuild barriers; no crypto-shredding-only acceptance. |
| `REOPEN-PROVIDER-ECONOMICS` | Current actual license/provider terms and dated quotes, integer-minor-unit/currency economics, numeric limits and explicit spending approval, not invented costs. |
| `REOPEN-PURPOSE-REVIEW` | Explicit new dated, independently reviewed, protected-merged superseding decision and policy-version change, preserving purpose, sharing and authoritative-money boundaries. |

Reversal requires that **new explicit approved decision**, its real authority
and versioned consequences. Do not delete ADR-025, repurpose another allocation,
edit an accepted record without a later date, or toggle an ALLOWED value into
this prohibited-only schema. Existing crypto, erasure, sharing and egress
decisions remain controlling; any intentional change to them needs its own
properly scoped decision.

A later separately reviewed persistence implementation starts **default OFF**.
Reopening alone enables nothing. `EMBEDDING-DEFAULT-OFF-ACCEPTANCE` requires the
artifact's complete named activation checks: actual accepted-policy gate
consumption; tenant and cross-purpose denial; full model-generation re-index;
zero post-erasure similarity-query residue; retention/export/backup/restore and
provider-copy erasure; reviewed inversion/membership thresholds; independent
Core/QA/Security/Privacy review; and explicit spend/usage limits.
These are future requirements, **not passed tests**.

The original rollback condition remains: remove serving access first, prevent
writers/rebuilds, then schedule and verify hard deletion of the permitted
implementation's copies before removing it. Retain required incident/audit
evidence without vectors or source text. This decision has no serving deployment
to roll back and does not claim a cleanup rehearsal.
